newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Coffee - Brazil crop forecasts start to blossom.
newsitem.headline: Coffee - Brazil crop forecasts start to blossom.

text.p: Brazilian provisional estimates of the 1997/98 coffee harvest are just beginning to crop up but it is already clear there is going to be a wider range of estimates than at this stage last year.
On Thursday the Minas Gerais State Agricultural Federation (Faemg) estimated the 1997/98 state harvest at 8.3 million 60-kg bags, down 40 percent from a revised 1996/97 figure of 13.8 million bags.
The estimate was announced by the president of the National Agricultural Confederation (CNA), Rui Queiroz, who said that the survey was "an offical figure based on statistics".
He also said that the CNA was working with a figure of 18 million bags for the total Brazilian harvest but this was just an "informal projection", he said.

The 18 million bags was using the 8.3 million bags for Minas Gerais, 3.5 million bags for Espirito Santo, 2.3 million for Sao Paulo, 1.9 million for Parana and two million bags for other states such as Rondonia and Bahia, Quieroz said.
One other producer group which has come out with a forecast of below 20 million bags is the Caccer association of growers in the Cerrado region of Minas Gerais state.
Last month, Caccer said it expected the forthcoming harvest to be 17.8 million bags, a figure which was met with scepticism from other sections of the coffee community.
Last week the Guaxupe cooperative in Minas Gerais said that the most optimistic scenario was for a crop of 20 million bags.

It cited a preliminary forecast by Jose Braz Matiello, coordinator for the Ministry of Agriculture's Procafe section, of 19.2 million bags, in which Matiello plotted Minas production at 8.5 million bags.

One of the problems this year has been the erratic flowerings in some areas which is making it more difficult for agronomists to gauge future production, said Luiz Moricochi of the Sao Paulo state Instititute for Agricultural Economics.
"Everyone has a different figure. I can make a stab at it like everyone else when I say it should be between 20 million and 22 million bags but we are only making rough forecasts," Moricochi said.
"But this just shows how important it is that we have a scientific survey carried out," he added.
The government has already said that it wants to set up a forecasting system and this should be one of the priorities of the new coffee council, the CDPC, which is to decide future coffee policy.

However the council still has to have its first meeting, only now expected to take place in January, which means that any forecast is unlikely to be ready before the second quarter of this year, dealers said.
While growers seem to be looking at around 20 million bags, traders seem to be preferring the 24 million bag level.
Earlier this month, Santos export firm Icatu/Sumatra said it was expecting a crop of 24 million bags from an upwardly revised 27.65 million bags in 1996/97.

Francisco Ourique, director of Flavour Coffee, is working on the basis of a 23.6 million bag crop, allowing for 11.5 million bags in Minas Gerais, four million in Espirito Santo, three million in Sao Paulo, 2.1 million in Parana and one million each for Rondonia, Bahia and other states.
One other issue is what in fact was the size of the 1996/97 crop, especially in the light of Faemg's 1.4 million bag increase in its harvest estimate from a previous figure of 12.4 million bags.
"It's all very well talking about percentage drops from this year but on what - 22 million, 24 million or 26 million bags," Moricochi said.
When Faemg announced its 12.42 million bag estimate in the middle of August, the government said it was reducing its own working figure to between 24 million to 25 million bags.
The upward revision in the Minas Gerais forecast should in theory therefore bring this figure closer to the 26 million to 27 million bags now being used by many traders.
-- Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
